title: First Flame
snippet:
First Flame -  Dark Souls - storyline - age_of_fire 
 age_of_fire : With the dragons defeated, the Lords took over the world, ruling as Gods from their seat of power in the land of Lordran. It was a prosperous era, and many nations were born. In time, however, the First Flame began to fade, and with it the power of the Gods, leading to an era of decay and the emergence of the Undead Curse. If the Flame were to gutter out completely, it would end the Age of Fire and bring about the Age of Dark.

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Talk with Yuria at Firelink Shrine and exhaust her dialogue.
The questline is now complete: After defeating the Soul of Cinder, simply interact with the First Flame to trigger this ending.
** The infobox will say "Link the First Flame" even after the questline is completed; this is expected. If the player wishes to ensure that the Usurpation ending will be triggered, they may return to Firelink Shrine at any time and talk to Yuria. Unless she voices her displeasure with the Ashen One, this will confirm that The Usurpation of Fire ending will take place upon interacing with the First Flame instead of the To Link the First Flame ending.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: The idea that the linking of the First Flame was unnatural and that it ran contrary to the order of the world is an important concept in the *Dark Souls* series, especially as the Age of Fire is prolonged perpetually by innumerable successive individuals seeking to prevent the coming of the Age of Dark.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In Ending 2: "The End of Fire", the First Flame is snuffed out, albeit with the Fire Keeper revealing that one day "tiny flames will dance across the darkness", which suggests that the First Flame partially perseveres in the form of embers within the Lords of Cinder of the past. As these Lords will use these embers of the First Flame to exert influence the world, this Age of Dark does not spell finality for the Flame. Alternatively, the player can choose to intervene as the Fire Keeper is about to extinguish the First Flame, by killing her before the cinematic ends. In this ending, the Ashen One instead takes the First Flame for themselves while the final segment of the opening narration is heard: *"Nameless, accursed Undead, unfit even to be cinder...And so it is...that Ash seeketh embers."*

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Ending (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - availability_2 
 availability_2 : {'name': 'Ending', 'description': 'Having witnessed visions of a world without the First Flame, the summoned Fire Keeper takes the First Flame into her hands, where she lets it wither and die out entirely. The light in the sky quickly fades together with the Flame and soon as the world descends into complete darkness, ending the Age of Fire.\n\nAlthough the world has now entered the long-postponed Age of Dark which would have naturally succeeded Fire had Lord Gwyn not started the tradition of linking the First Flame prior to the original *Dark Souls*. The shape that this new Age of Dark will take, and the part that the Unkindled One will play within it, are left unclear.'}

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Although the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods lasted for centuries, at some point the First Flame began to fade. Gwyn understood that if the Flame went out, the Age of Fire would be succeeded by an Age of Dark, a new order of humans led by a Dark Lord. Fearful of this outcome, the god made a drastic decision: In order to maintain the order of Gods, he would sacrifice himself to link the dying Flame and prolong its life. He trusted none but himself to carry out the sacrifice involved; he thus divided the power of his Lord Soul among the members of his clan and handed down the power of the sun to his children, leaving his firstborn son to inherit his titles. Gwyn also tasked his sons and Frampt with shepherding the humans into following his example, linking the Flame generation after generation, to uphold his Age of Fire, each of them becoming Lords through the process.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
As the games progresses, the sun itself starts to change, until it eerily resembles the Darksign itself.

At the end of the game, after defeating the Soul of Cinder, the Ashen One, in case they chose to link the First Flame, is covered from head to toe in a soft-looking fire, unlike the flaming inferno of the first game. The implications are clear: The First Flame itself now is so weak that it cannot be kindled anymore.

The First Flame, as the Age of Fire, is beyond saving.

In *The Ringed City*, it is implied that the unnatural prolonging of the Age of Fire has caused irrepairable damage to the world, as is shown after Filianore's awakening: the fertile lands seen when the Ashen One arrived in the city are replaced by a seemingly unending, as-far-the-eye-can-see's barren wasteland of unknown nature.

title: First Flame
snippet: Desperate to ensure that their Age of Fire continued, and afraid of the coming Dark, the Lords did everything they could to keep the First Flame lit. Gwyn's clan linked the sacred bonfires that were tied to the Flame to humanity, and shepherded the humans who worshipped them to kindle the flames. The Witch of Izalith attempted to use her own powerful soul to create a new First Flame, but this attempt failed, instead creating the perverse Flame of Chaos and transforming the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, which would go on to birth the race of Demons.

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Ending (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - ending_2 
 ending_2 : The Ashen One strikes the Fire Keeper down before the First Flame is completely extinguished, then tramples her limp body and takes the First Flame from her hands. Kneeling, the Ashen One raises the Flame towards the sun obscured by a fire-dripping eclipse that resembles the Darksign.

Although the meaning of this ending is ambiguous, it likely symbolizes that the Ashen One acquires the power of the First Flame's power for themselves rather than in accordance with any of the great powers at play. The Usurpation of Fire ending also sees the Ashen One acquiring the First Flame rather than link it or let it die, although the absence of the followers of Londor in this ending hints that the Ashen One's plans are their own.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : The are characters who have linked the First Flame throughout the history of the *Dark Souls* universe.

To "link the First Flame" is to reach it, be powerful enough to withstand its power, and rekindle the flame anew; it is done in order to stop the First Flame from withering out and dying, a process that occurs naturally over time and would mean both the end of the Age of Fire and the coming of an Age of Dark. To attempt to link the flame, one must typically reach the kiln built around the First Flame and defeat the empty husk of the previous Lords of Cinders guarding it against those not worthy of its power.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
***Ash Seeketh Embers**: If the Ashen One gave the Eyes of a Fire Keeper to the Fire Keeper, they may summon her upon defeating the Soul of Cinder. The Fire Keeper will take the First Flame into her hands. Before the flames fade, the Ashen One may strike her down. The Ashen One steps over the limp body of the Fire Keeper and takes the First Flame into their own hands. Kneeling, the Ashen One raises the flame, offering it to the Darksign Sun.
***The Usurpation of Fire**: If the Ashen One allowed Yoel to draw out their true strength a sufficient amount of times through the Dark Sigil, followed Yuria's instructions and "married" Anri, the Ashen One may, instead of linking the fire, absorb it into themselves. The Ashen One collapses from the strain and awakens before a Darksign Sun turned white, and also finds Yuria, Anri, and an army of hollows greeting them as their Lord and praying for the Ashen One to make Londor whole.

title: First Flame
snippet: By the time of *Dark Souls III*, many other such sacrifices, who have become posthumously known as Lords of Cinder, have given themselves to the First Flame, and the Age of Fire has persevered for many generations as a result. However, when the latest individual chosen for the honour, Prince Lothric, abandons his duty by refusing to link the fire, a desperate attempt to save the fading Flame begins. Four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected to link the fire once more, however - aside from Ludleth of Courland - they too choose to flee their duties, forcing the Ashen One to drag them back.

title: First Flame
snippet:
Aware that time was quickly running out for his kingdom, Gwyn and a detachment of his knights entered the Kiln of the First Flame. The knights stood guard as Gwyn sacrificed himself to the waning Flame at the Kiln's centre. This immediately reinvigorated the First Flame, creating a firestorm that turned the Kiln to ash, and incinerated all of Gwyn's knights, creating the Black Knights and dooming them to wander the lands as disembodied spirits forever after.

Gwyn's sacrifice succeeded in perpetuating the Age of Fire for a time, but *Dark Souls* takes place at least 1000 years later, and the Flame is quickly fading once again. Soon, only Dark will remain.

title: Fire Keeper (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
If given the eyes of the first Fire Keeper, she sees a world without fire, and is frightened by the mere thought of it. Even so, she is willing to end the cycle permanently if the Ashen One requests it. If the Ashen One chooses to realize her dream, she will be summoned to the Kiln of the First Flame. At that time, she will hold the First Flame in her hands and let it die out, thus unlocking the End of Fire ending. If the Ashen One chooses to succumb to their desire, and kill her during the ritual; the power of the First Flame would fall to their hands.

The Fire Keeper can also be talked to, and her dialogue changes throughout the course of the game.

She will psychically respond to most gestures performed by the player.

If killed, she will always respawn at Firelink Shrine, stating that as a Fire Keeper, she cannot die.

title: First Flame
snippet: But then, somewhere in the hollows deep underground, a great and primordial fire that would come to be known as the First Flame burst into being. In doing so, it brought disparities into the world for the first time, such as heat and cold, life and death, and light and dark. Soon, humanoid creatures emerged from the darkness surrounding the First Flame, attracted by the fire. These creatures found sources of power called souls near the Flame, and took on the diverse powers the souls gave them. With the strength of four particularly powerful souls, four figures were born: Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith, Gwyn, the Lord of Sunlight, and the Furtive Pygmy. Using their newfound power, these Lords and their forces overthrew the ancient dragons, ushering in the Age of Fire.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: Although the system that managed the linking of the First Flame had rung the bells to resurrect the past Lords of Cinder when needed, not all of them have awakened from their resting places. Consequently, once the Flame eventually goes out, at some point these Lords of Cinder from the past will rise again and wander the lands like tiny flames. These beings will possess fragments of the First Flame stored within their bodies in the form of cinders, giving them the powers of the Flame in a world that will be enveloped in Darkness.

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Ending (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - ending 
 ending : Fulfilling the purpose for which they were brought back to life, the Ashen One links the First Flame and becomes a Lord of Cinder. The Flame connects with their body, slowly setting them ablaze as they sit beside the bonfire.

Although in theory, this leads to a continuation of the once-glorious Age of Fire, this linking of the Flame is but a shadow of the linking as can be performed by the Chosen Undead in *Dark Souls*, echoing the significant weakening of the First Flame, which instead of engulfing the Kiln into an explosive blaze of fire remains weak, barely kindled anew. The world remains dim and covered in ash, with the sun still obscured by a fire-dripping eclipse that resembles the Darksign, further exemplifying that this prolonged Age of Fire will pale when compared to days of old.

title: Courland
snippet: At a certain point the First Flame began to fade again and the first Fire Keeper of Lothric had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a "barren plane of endless darkness". For this reason, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition, was called to become a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Defying his frail appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Champion, something for which he himself expresses remorse and asks to be forgiven. Despite his role, Ludleth was then exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric, ensuring that the first Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes and that all future maidens like her were deprived of their sight, to prevent them from observing the future without the light of the First Flame. The original eyes were hidden in a version of the Firelink Shrine on the verge of sinking into darkness and where the First Flame was an

title: Ashen One
snippet: ***The End of Fire**: If the Ashen One gave the Eyes of a Fire Keeper to the Fire Keeper, they may summon her upon defeating the Soul of Cinder. The Fire Keeper will take the First Flame into her hands. She states that the fire quickly fades and that dark will soon settle, but predicts that one day, tiny flames will dance across the darkness, like embers linked by lords past, suggesting that the other Lords of Cinder of the past will one day rise and wander through the darkness with their own fragments of the First Flame. As the absolute darkness settles upon the world, the Fire Keeper asks if the Ashen One can still hear her.

title: Lothric
snippet: In the beginning, the first Fire Keeper had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a barren plane of endless darkness. Acting to ward off an Age of Dark, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition of Courland, rose to the challenge of becoming a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Despite his feeble appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Lord, something for which he himself expresses remorse, asking to be forgiven. Ludleth was exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric to ensure that the Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes, as well as all future maidens, to prevent them from observing a future without the Flame. The original eyes were sealed away in an enigmatic instance of Firelink Shrine, where the First Flame had all but gone out.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
The original Lord of Cinder was Gwyn, although more would link the flame and extend the Age of Fire in subsequent eras. Becoming a Lord of Cinder entails a sacrifice, as the Lord is consumed by the First Flame in the process. After Gwyn linked the flame, only his mere husk defended it; with each subsequent linking of the Flame, remnants of each new Lord of Cinder would merge with the previous ones' and strengthen the First Flame's guardian, eventually taking the form of the Soul of Cinder.

Throughout history, countless aspiring Lords were lost attempting to reach the Flame; among those who succeeded, some ultimately lacked the strength to withstand its power, and were burned to ash by the Flame instead of linking it. These individuals came to be known as Unkindled: ill-fated champions who were buried in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard which scarcely saw any visitors.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: However, it becomes apparent that at this stage in the Age of Fire, which has been unnaturally prolonged far beyond its intended length, there is little that can be done to keep the First Flame lit. Even if the Ashen One chooses to link the Flame, the fire that results from this rebirth is small and feeble in comparison to the raging inferno that resulted from the Chosen Undead linking the Flame in *Dark Souls*.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, the First Flame is so weakened that Lords of Cinder past are resurrected so that the embers of the First Flame inside them serve as fuel for new Linkings. Prince Lothric, who was raised to become the next Lord of Cinder, refused to Link the First Flame, while three of the resurrected Lords of Cinder refused to be used as fuel, leading to resurrection of several Unkindled in the hopes that one of them might slay the fleeting Lords of Cinder and Lothric, and Link the First Flame.

title: Humans
snippet: Over time, others would repeat Gwyn's sacrifice—either for their own reasons or to follow in his footsteps—to rekindle the First Flame. As the First Flame was not intended to burn as long as it had, the fabric of reality began to suffer.

title: Farron Follower
snippet: As the First Flame continued to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, the Lords of Cinder of the past were exhumed from their graves to once again be used as fuel. Among them the Abyss Watchers too rose from their graves, but refused to sacrifice themselves again to link the Fire, choosing to return to their Keep in Farron. However, the Followers were no longer present to cull the warriors that would become corrupted by the Abyss, consequently forcing the Watchers to do so themselves, wasting their strength to kill each other to contain the spreading corruption.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

Calling it "futile" is a euphemism: the unnatural prolonging of the First Flame's lifespan came with disastrous, if not, downright catastrophical proportions: when the Lords of Cinder started to resurrect, somehow, portions of their countries and homelands were, literally, "teleported" to Lothric, changing the landscape in unpredictable ways.

By the time *Dark Souls 3* takes place, the damage caused to the world by the unnatural prolonging of the Age of Fire seems to be irreversible.

As the games progresses, the sun itself starts to change, until it eerily resembles the Darksign itself.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: Following the failure of this first contingency plan, a second plan is activated: Unkindled, those who had previously tried to link the First Flame but who had failed to do so, are resurrected from their graves in the Cemetery of Ash, and tasked with placing the rebellious Lords of Cinder upon their thrones so that the First Flame might be linked once more. The Ashen One, protagonist of *Dark Souls III*, is one of these Unkindled. After the Ashen One defeats each of the Lords of Cinder and places their remains upon their respective thrones in the Firelink Shrine, the Fire Keeper removes the embers of the Lords and bestows them upon the Ashen One, making them a "true lord, fit to link the fire," and imbuing them with the power to proceed to the Kiln of the First Flame.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, who was raised to become a Lord of Cinder, refused to link the First Flame. This led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves: these Lords were meant to sacrifice themselves to the Flame once again, using what little embers remained within themselves as kindling. However, most of these Lords refused the call, and instead settled back into their domains. To prevent the First Flame from dying out, the Unkindled would then be resurrected as a last resort; these Champions were bound to seek the absconded Lords of Cinder, and forcefully bring them back—in the form of their cinders—to their empty thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once all five Lords "sat" their thrones, an Unkindled Champion would be bestowed the embers of these Lords, and sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to overcome the final challenge and link the Flame.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Gwyn's act of linking the First Flame came to be a point of controversy for several figures; namely Kaathe and Aldia would regard Gwyn's sacrifice as having "unnaturally" extended an Age of Fire that was never meant to last, inhibiting the potential of humans in the process. As of the time of the Chosen Undead, one consequence of Kaathe's actions lies beneath Firelink Shrine: the ruins of New Londo, which was captured by the Darkstalker and had to be flooded before the Abyss within could spread to the surface world.

title: Bonfire Ascetic
snippet:
Bonfire Ascetic -  Dark Souls II - item - general_information 
 general_information : When burned, a Bonfire Ascetic will change the entire bonfire area to the next playthrough level. For example, if used during the first playthrough, it will bump the difficulty to New Game+, and if used at New Game++, it will bump the difficulty to New Game+++. This process is irreversible and persists on following playthroughs. For example, if an area was increased to New Game+ on one's first playthrough, it will be at New Game++ difficulty on the next playthrough.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Now bereft of most of his Lord Soul's power and with only the power of his soul, Gwyn left for the Kiln of the First Flame, the structure built to house and protect it, with only his robes, his mighty greatsword and his powerless crown, accompanied only by a guard of Black Knights. Eventually Gwyn linked the First Flame, prolonging its life but himself being consumed by it, reduced to the empty husk of cinders guarding the core of the Kiln. The inferno of the newly kindled fire melted the surroundings and burned his knights to ashes, leaving them to wander the world as disembodied spirits.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lothric, Younger Prince: A prince brought into the world by the royal family of Lothric for the sole purpose of linking the Flame; however, his frailty, curse and suffering led him to reject his destiny.
Ashen One: An Unkindled who was resurrected in Lothric with the duty of linking of the First Flame, overcame multiple challenges and gathered the cinders of Lords of the past before gaining access to the Kiln of the First Flame.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In *Dark Souls III*, countless beings have prolonged the Age of Fire, preventing its end and holding off the coming of the Age of Dark. By the time the game begins, there are countless Lords of Cinder - those who successfully linked the First Flame before - and even more Unkindled who were unsuccessful. Eventually the one anointed to next link the Flame (and indeed, who was born for that very purpose), Prince Lothric, rejected the idea that the Age of Fire should be prolonged any further and instead desired to end what he called the "fire-linking curse." A contingency plan was then activated, in which previous Lords of Cinder were resurrected in hopes that they, who had linked the First Flame before, might do so again. However, by this time, the world that had been created during the Age of Fire had become a twisted shadow of its former self. As a result of the prolonging of the current Age, the act of which seemingly constituted a rejection of the natural order, the material world

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet: The deformed Aldia is encountered several times by the Bearer of the Curse, to whom he imparts his extensive knowledge on the nature of life. He expresses outrage over the actions of the Lord of Light, who cursed humans into mortality and introduced the cycle of light and dark by linking the First Flame. Aldia's bleak worldview considers mankind as "props on the stage of life", persevering merely through obsession. While acknowledging the merits of the Age of Fire, he labels the roots of this "warm, resplendent" world as a lie, with the linking of the Fire as its original sin. Nevertheless, Aldia realizes that one could wish to inherit this order, even if built on a "tender, exquisite" lie. Instead of submission to the peace provided by the status quo, he offers a third "path"; obscure and unpaved, yet could perhaps ascend the scope of Light and Dark.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin at some point learned of Gwyn's existence and his story but not his name, referring to him merely as the "Lord of Light". He understood how Gwyn altered the natural order and began linking the Flame, which extended the Age of Fire against the course of nature, and he expresses his outrage at Gwyn for making men lesser than their original form as the "Lord of Light" banished Dark and all that stemmed from Humanity with the Darksign, defining it as the "First Sin" committed against humans and their nature.

title: Primordial Serpents
snippet: Even after possibly hundreds of thousands years after the first linking of the Flame, Frampt (or other serpents affiliated with his ideology) continued to propagate the cult of the linking of the Flame; influencing kingdoms, rulers and simple Undead to continue the tradition started by Gwyn. When the First Flame drifted up to position itself on the nascent kingdom of Lothric, Frampt or other serpents affiliated with his ideology reached the city too. Over time the serpents passed on the culture of linking the Flame to the royal family of Lothric, pushing them to preserve the tradition and actively produce heirs capable of becoming Lords of Cinder. Frampt or his kin were represented in numerous statues, on par with the Three Pillars of Lothric, with elegant clothes and angel wings, showing their central role within the kingdom, considered "divine messengers". Following Prince Lothric's refusal to link the Flame and the disappearance of King Oceiros, the fate of the primordial serpents

title: Chosen Undead
snippet:
Chosen Undead -  Dark Souls - character - epilogue 
 epilogue : After offering the necessary Lord Souls, the doors to the Kiln of the First Flame are opened to the Chosen Undead. Gwyn, now reduced to a Lord of Cinder, breathes his last breath in the final confrontation with the Chosen Undead. It is here that the Chosen Undead may make their decision of either linking the flame or walking away from it. Depending on which course of action is taken, one of the two possible endings will be unlocked. Whether the player has aligned themselves with Kaathe or Frampt will not affect the ending of the game.

***Link the Fire:** This ending is unlocked if the player rekindles the First Flame. The Chosen Undead offers themselves as kindling to the fire. Sacrificing all of their souls, the Chosen Undead is consumed by the flames and the Age of Fire is extended, as life is breathed into the First Flame once more.

 dark_souls_iii_the_last_days_of_the_fire : (The events before Dark Souls III)

Over the centuries, dozens of people link themselves to the First Flame, becoming Lords of Cinder
The souls of all those who have linked the First Flame manifest in the form of the Soul of Cinder, an entity possessing all the abilities of the previous Lords of Cinder even if it's just an empty husk.
This manifestation of the previous Lords of Cinder exists as the First Flame's last defense from future linkers
The future Lords of Cinder face the Soul of Cinder at the Kiln of the First Flame before they can link the First Flame

Due to the First Flame naturally dying out, time and space slowly converge towards it, bringing the various regions of the world towards the Kiln of the First Flame

title: Oceiros, the Consumed King
snippet: When the royal family realized that Lothric would not improve from his condition, they resorted to repulsive acts in an attempt to obtain a worthy Champion for the linking, even if it meant to create something inhuman: the rulers bound the souls of the two princes together with a curse. Although the exact motive behind this act is unknown, it is likely that the rulers intended for Prince Lothric to draw out some of the strength of his elder brother's soul, potentially making them worthy Champions for the First Flame together. The resulting Soul of the Twin Princes was suitable kindling for the First Flame, even as the princes were physically incapable of overcoming the obstacles involved in linking the Flame. Unable and unwilling to fulfill their destiny, the princes retreated to their chamber to await the end of the world.

title: Lothric
snippet: When the royal family realized that Lothric would not improve from his condition, they resorted to repulsive acts in an attempt to obtain a worthy Champion for the linking: the rulers bound the souls of the two princes together with a curse. Although the exact motive behind this act is unknown, it is likely that the rulers intended for Prince Lothric to draw out some of the strength of his elder brother's soul, which could have allowed him to qualify as worthy Ash for the First Flame. It was even said that Lorian willingly submitted to the curse, even as it crippled him. The resulting Soul of the Twin Princes was one worthy of providing kindling for the First Flame, even as the princes were physically incapable of overcoming the obstacles involved in linking the Flame. Unable and unwilling to fulfill their destiny, the princes retreated to their chamber to await the end of the world.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet: She eventually became wife to King Oceiros, the last monarch of Lothric, and supported the kingdom's desire to produce an heir worthy of linking the First Flame, giving birth first to Elder Prince Lorian, raised to become a knight, and Younger Prince Lothric, expected to become a "champion" and sacrifice himself to the Flame. However, when Prince Lothric and his brother refused to link the fading Flame and they chose to wait out the end of the Age of Fire, King Oceiros went mad in his attempt to produce an heir worthy of their sacrificial destiny. The king discovered the heretical faith of the paledrake Seath among the scholars of the Grand Archives and became convinced that a crossbreed heir would have the strength to link the Flame. Oceiros eventually became a deformed humanoid dragon and with him the queen had her youngest child, Ocelotte. After producing the potential champion, Gwynevere quietly disappeared from the kingdom of Lothric. Realizing that the Flame would soon go out

title: Darksign
snippet:
Darksign -  Dark Souls II - item - lore 
 lore : Gwyn had foreseen the Age of Dark at the end of the Age of Fire and, fearing the infinite potential of the Dark Soul that the Furtive Pygmy found and the Humanity that inherited it, he forced a ring of fire around the Dark Soul to contain its powers and making every new human assume a weakened form and bear the Darksign. In addition, various groups were created to encourage worshipping Gwyn and his kin as Gods, such as the Way of White, the oldest and most powerful cultural organization centered around the veneration of the gods of Anor Londo, who spread Miracles to humans and cultivated the cult of the Age of Fire and the linking of the Flame.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Studying and experimenting on the inhuman creatures and their souls, and via studies on artifacts from older kingdoms, Vendrick and Aldia pioneered the creation of Golems, very similar in appearance to the captured giants. Vendrick made Nashandra his queen, and had the golems build his Royal Castle, as proof of his gratitude and affection to her. Beneath the royal castle was the ancient Throne of Want, an artifact capable of connecting to the First Flame, the source of souls and beginning of all that the king was seeking. Studying the First Flame and the mysteries of the soul with his brother Aldia, the king acquired a profound understanding of the history of the world and the rules of reality, how the Flame brought Disparity and everything from it, propagating souls in the world every time someone linked it, giving it new strength. He also understood how the Dark was kept under control as long as the fire flourished, and that once the fire naturally weakened the curse would strike

title: Dark Lord
snippet:
Dark Lord -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : **This section of the lore lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations**

The Dark Lords are beings who were meant to become Lords of Cinder, but refused to link the First Flame and extend the Age of Fire, with the specific intent of bringing forth the Age of Dark (also referred to as an "Age of Man"). Dark Lords, while powerful enough to overcome the trials involved in linking the Flame, apparently don't have to inherit a primordial force (such as the First Flame) in order to be deemed worthy of their title. For instance, if the Chosen Undead chooses to become a Dark Lord, abandoning the power of the First Flame, several primordial serpents will nevertheless bow before their new Lord (including both Kaathe and Frampt), even as the Chosen Undead lacks the extraordinary power granted by the Flame.

title: The Nameless King
snippet: After his father Gwyn left to link the First Flame, the throne of Anor Londo would pass to the eldest son of the King; and so the Nameless King inherited the Sunlight of his father. He would thus wear the golden crown, and succeed his father's titles of "king of the gods" and "god of the sun". The Nameless King was said to be inferior to none in terms of military strength. Gwyn's firstborn preserved his father's design and instructions, shepherding humans on the path to the Linking of the First Flame to continue the Age of Fire. In fact, underneath Anor Londo, a city was built exclusively for the undead, with an altar inside for the firstborn of Gwyn, and the aim of guiding a chosen undead who would one day sacrifice themselves to the Flame. Inside the city was the Undead Parish, a church at the center of the cult of the burg and connected to the first test to start on the path of Firelinking and ring the first Bell of Awakening. Furthermore, the town was connected to the Firelink

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet:
Witch of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : The name of the Witch is literally **Izalith**, as stated by Quelana in the Japanese version, where she calls the Witch "my mother Izalith".
During her dialogue, Quelana mentions that most humans are unable to perceive her, and implies that they absolutely cannot, so long as she actively does not want them to.
Despite herself being consumed by the Chaos Flame, Izalith was partially successful in replicating the First Flame. Not only does Chaos generate life, it also has its own fire-linking quality, wherein a demon Champion is destined to rekindle it, becoming the Demon Prince. This system parallels the prophecy of the Chosen Undead and their becoming a Lord of Cinder.

title: Timeline
snippet:
The Ashen One defeats the Soul of Cinder and gains access to the First Flame
The Ashen One understands that linking the Fire again won't save the world this time but also that letting it die out in the current state of the world and humans would only lead to the Age of the Deep, in which humanity and the Dark Soul would be putrid and stagnated
The Ashen One usurps the First Flame, ripping it from its kiln and absorbing it into their Dark Sigil, ascending to Dark Lord
The Dark Lord, in control of the First Flame, is able to manipulate space and time and can start the true Age of Humanity, becoming its deity and guide with the Sable Church and Londor as their servants and followers.

title: Crown of the Great Lord
snippet:
Crown of the Great Lord -  Dark Souls - armor - description 
 description : Crown of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, who linked the First Flame.

Lord Gwyn, bearer of the ultimate soul, divided that power among his great clan before linking the flame. But he did keep his crown, perhaps to preserve a symbol of the monarch, for its actual power had fully subsided.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: Through another questline, the player can cooperate with Yuria, a leader of the Sable Church of Londor, who urges the Ashen One to take the Flame for themselves, to usher in an Age of Dark; for the Sisters of the Sable Church were under the guidance of Kaathe. This is Ending 4: "The Usurpation of Fire", where the Flame is wrested by the Ashen One, who is to lead the Age of Man as the Lord of Hollows. By the time of *Dark Souls III*, the undead curse has been accepted by the people of Londor, who have come to view it as a blessing, and their Hollow form as the "true face of man".
